props.title: The Affair of the Necklace
props.initialSlug: A queen's jewels spark scandal in pre-Revolution France

sections.content: Set against the opulent backdrop of pre-revolutionary France, **The Affair of the Necklace** (2001) fits into a fascinating subset of historical dramas that explore how seemingly minor scandals precipitated massive political upheavals. Like **Marie Antoinette** (2006) and **Ridicule** (1996), it captures the decadent excess of Versailles while hinting at the simmering unrest that would soon explode. Hilary Swank's portrayal of Jeanne de la Motte-Valois brings complexity to a historical figure often dismissed as a mere con artist, similar to how **The Favourite** (2018) rehabilitated previously maligned court figures.

sections.content: The film's attention to period detail and costume design follows in the tradition of meticulous historical dramas like **Amadeus** (1984) and **Barry Lyndon** (1975). However, where it truly shines is in depicting the labyrinthine nature of court intrigue, showing how reputation and appearance could make or break someone's standing. This theme of appearances versus reality would later be explored more satirically in **Farewell, My Queen** (2012) and **A Royal Affair** (2012).

While the film received mixed reviews upon release, it represents an important entry in the historical con artist genre, predating similar films like **The Other Boleyn Girl** (2008) and **The Young Victoria** (2009). Its exploration of class mobility and feminine power within rigid social structures remains relevant, though later films like **Portrait of a Lady on Fire** (2019) would handle these themes with more nuance. sections.content: The film's backdrop of brewing revolution connects it to a larger tradition of films about aristocratic decline, from **The Leopard** (1963) to **The Last Emperor** (1987). Its depiction of nobility's disconnect from reality while standing on the precipice of massive social change echoes themes later explored in **Les Misérables** (2012) and **Restoration** (1995).
